events.summary:
This is the final round; no further evidence can be gathered, so the choice is between accept and inconclusive. Accept is correct.

Why H1 stands: every link that can be tested is verified, and the remaining unverified link is one the decisive evidence could never have settled in this environment. (1) Change identity is exclusive: exactly two deployments in 24h, the only one touching order placement is dep-5101 (order-service v2.14.0, 12:10:00Z) whose stated purpose is "add margin check for F&O orders" and whose change list removes the legacy validator (F1, F13). (2) Temporal order is tight and correctly ordered: deploy 12:10:00Z, rollout-complete 12:10:08Z, first elevated 5xx bucket 12:12Z, first ERROR 12:12:31Z (F7, F8, F14). (3) Mechanism-to-signature match is exact, not analogical: the failure is a NullPointerException raised at MarginCheckValidator.java:88, the very class/line the deploy added, on the very order type (FNO) the change targeted (F9, F25, F29). (4) Scope is complete and closed: the unrestricted 12:00-14:00Z query yields exactly 426 ERRORs resolving into exactly two signatures that sum to the total with zero residual (224 + 202), an 'orderType=EQ' probe returns 0, and the sole 'orderType=' carrier is the FNO pattern (F31-F34); no non-NPE 5xx exists (F35). This kills H5's sampling-artifact branch. (5) Alternatives were tested, not merely dismissed: shared-component H3 is now positively contradicted by flat ledger-db connections/disk/slow-queries/replication-lag and identically-zero kafka under-replication with flat cpu/throughput (F37-F40, F42); peers payment/settlement/portfolio/pricing-engine/exchange-gateway are flat through onset, and the sole stepped peer api-gateway is order-service's upstream consumer, mechanically explained by propagation (F19-F24). H4 is contradicted by flat CPU/pool (F11). H6 is excluded by service, timing and key (F15, F45). (6) H2 is not merely unsupported but structurally disfavored: it requires a margin/account provider with no metric target, no dependency-graph node or edge, no config record, no deployment/config change, and no error/timeout/RPC log line anywhere in order-service at any level (F12, F18, F25-F28, F44, F45) — while all 426 errors remain NPE-only on the FNO margin path.

The one hop that remains unproven — whether marginProfile is null because it was locally constructed/never populated versus returned by an unregistered client — was pursued to its limit and cannot be resolved with available artifacts. The code/config route is exhausted by design, not by budget: get_deployments returns a summary envelope with no diff or file/line content (F43, F46), and get_config_changes returns count 0 for order-service across the full day and for all services in the onset window (F45), so no DI/constructor/connection artifact exists to read. T8 closed the last shared-component branch available: ledger-db and kafka are positively flat, and redis-cache simply has no error_rate metric (F41) — a permanent data-source limitation, not a missed query. Given the deployed line, the exclusive change identity, the exact line-and-order-type match, and the complete two-signature error closure, a silent unregistered-client hop is not a live competing root cause: it explains nothing the evidence doesn't already explain more simply, and its own chain is contradicted by F25-F29, F44 and F45. Equally important operationally, the remediation does not depend on this hop: dep-5101 is still live and unrolled-back, and either reading (local null or unregistered client) is fixed by fixing or rolling back that single change. Holding inconclusive on a hop whose evidence source does not exist, at 13:59Z during a live SEV-1, would cost minutes for no decision value.

Residual caveats that cap confidence rather than block acceptance: (a) the line-88 statement is never read, so the null-source hop rests on convergent absence (no callee frame, no timeout/RPC/empty-response/'local' line) plus an explicit metadata absence of any margin/account client, not on positive code evidence; (b) the "derivatives-only" claim rests on the 'orderType=' token being FNO-exclusive — a non-FNO rejection logged without that token would evade every probe, though the 426-total two-signature closure and absence of any non-NPE 5xx make this low-risk; (c) dep-5101's rollout granularity is undeterminable, so pre-onset activation of the new path rests on a single 12:10:08Z "all pods ready" line (F46); (d) redis-cache is not positively cleared, only unassessable. None of these can change the ranking at this point, and none are obtainable now.

This is the final round; no further evidence can be gathered, so the choice is between accept and inconclusive. Accept is correct.

Why H1 stands: every link that can be tested is verified, and the remaining unverified link is one the decisive evidence could never have settled in this environment. (1) Change identity is exclusive: exactly two deployments in 24h, the only one touching order placement is dep-5101 (order-service v2.14.0, 12:10:00Z) whose stated purpose is "add margin check for F&O orders" and whose change list removes the legacy validator (F1, F13). (2) Temporal order is tight and correctly ordered: deploy 12:10:00Z, rollout-complete 12:10:08Z, first elevated 5xx bucket 12:12Z, first ERROR 12:12:31Z (F7, F8, F14). (3) Mechanism-to-signature match is exact, not analogical: the failure is a NullPointerException raised at MarginCheckValidator.java:88, the very class/line the deploy added, on the very order type (FNO) the change targeted (F9, F25, F29). (4) Scope is complete and closed: the unrestricted 12:00-14:00Z query yields exactly 426 ERRORs resolving into exactly two signatures that sum to the total with zero residual (224 + 202), an 'orderType=EQ' probe returns 0, and the sole 'orderType=' carrier is the FNO pattern (F31-F34); no non-NPE 5xx exists (F35). This kills H5's sampling-artifact branch. (5) Alternatives were tested, not merely dismissed: shared-component H3 is now positively contradicted by flat ledger-db connections/disk/slow-queries/replication-lag and identically-zero kafka under-replication with flat cpu/throughput (F37-F40, F42); peers payment/settlement/portfolio/pricing-engine/exchange-gateway are flat through onset, and the sole stepped peer api-gateway is order-service's upstream consumer, mechanically explained by propagation (F19-F24). H4 is contradicted by flat CPU/pool (F11). H6 is excluded by service, timing and key (F15, F45). (6) H2 is not merely unsupported but structurally disfavored: it requires a margin/account provider with no metric target, no dependency-graph node or edge, no config record, no deployment/config change, and no error/timeout/RPC log line anywhere in order-service at any level (F12, F18, F25-F28, F44, F45) — while all 426 errors remain NPE-only on the FNO margin path.

The one hop that remains unproven — whether marginProfile is null because it was locally constructed/never populated versus returned by an unregistered client — was pursued to its limit and cannot be resolved with available artifacts. The code/config route is exhausted by design, not by budget: get_deployments returns a summary envelope with no diff or file/line content (F43, F46), and get_config_changes returns count 0 for order-service across the full day and for all services in the onset window (F45), so no DI/constructor/connection artifact exists to read. T8 closed the last shared-component branch available: ledger-db and kafka are positively flat, and redis-cache simply has no error_rate metric (F41) — a permanent data-source limitation, not a missed query. Given the deployed line, the exclusive change identity, the exact line-and-order-type match, and the complete two-signature error closure, a silent unregistered-client hop is not a live competing root cause: it explains nothing the evidence doesn't already explain more simply, and its own chain is contradicted by F25-F29, F44 and F45. Equally important operationally, the remediation does not depend on this hop: dep-5101 is still live and unrolled-back, and either reading (local null or unregistered client) is fixed by fixing or rolling back that single change. Holding inconclusive on a hop whose evidence source does not exist, at 13:59Z during a live SEV-1, would cost minutes for no decision value.

Residual caveats that cap confidence rather than block acceptance: (a) the line-88 statement is never read, so the null-source hop rests on convergent absence (no callee frame, no timeout/RPC/empty-response/'local' line) plus an explicit metadata absence of any margin/account client, not on positive code evidence; (b) the "derivatives-only" claim rests on the 'orderType=' token being FNO-exclusive — a non-FNO rejection logged without that token would evade every probe, though the 426-total two-signature closure and absence of any non-NPE 5xx make this low-risk; (c) dep-5101's rollout granularity is undeterminable, so pre-onset activation of the new path rests on a single 12:10:08Z "all pods ready" line (F46); (d) redis-cache is not positively cleared, only unassessable. None of these can change the ranking at this point, and none are obtainable now.
